recent_posts.title: New to the web platform in April
recent_posts.summary: Chrome 147 and Firefox 150 shipped to stable in April 2026, bringing several new web platform features. Highlights include the contrast-color() CSS function reaching Baseline (returns black or white for maximum contrast against a given color), scroll-driven animation range properties becoming Baseline, the ariaNotify() method for screen reader announcements, auto sizes for lazy-loaded images, element-scoped view transitions, the CSS border-shape property for non-rectangular borders, SVG textPath path attribute support, modulepreload for JSON and CSS modules, and Math.sumPrecise. Beta releases (Chrome 148, Firefox 151, Safari 26.5) preview name-only container queries, lazy loading for video/audio, CSS container style queries, and the :open pseudo-class.

recent_posts.title: March 2026 Baseline monthly digest
recent_posts.summary: March 2026 saw several web platform features reach Baseline interoperability milestones. Newly available features include the math font-family for MathML, Iterator.concat() for combining iterables, readable byte streams for efficient binary data handling, the Reporting API for browser-level error notifications, WebTransport for low-latency HTTP/3 communication, and new text-indent keywords (each-line and hanging). A large set of features also reached the Widely available tier (30 months of interoperability), including CSS subgrid, contain-intrinsic-size, @counter-style, image-set(), link rel=modulepreload, hyphens properties, overflow media queries, navigator.storage, and device orientation events. The digest also highlights Rachel Andrew's talk on pragmatically choosing Baseline targets and a guide on adding Baseline status indicators to Eleventy sites.

recent_posts.title: February 2026 Baseline monthly digest
recent_posts.summary: February 2026 saw several web platform features reach Baseline milestones, meaning they are now supported across all major browser engines. New features include the CSS shape() function for defining complex clip paths using standard CSS syntax, the Trusted Types API for preventing DOM-based XSS attacks, JavaScript Map methods getOrInsert() and getOrInsertComputed() for ergonomic key-value handling, and Zstandard (zstd) as a new HTTP Content-Encoding option. Additionally, the dirname HTML attribute became Baseline Widely available, helping multilingual form handling. The post also notes the launch of Interop 2026, an initiative to improve cross-browser feature interoperability.

recent_posts.title: New to the web platform in March
recent_posts.summary: Chrome 146, Firefox 149, and Safari 26.4 shipped in March 2026 with notable new web platform features. Highlights include scroll-triggered animations and the trigger-scope property in Chrome 146, optional container query conditions (name-only @container) in Firefox 149 and Safari 26.4, the popover hint value in Firefox 149, grid-lanes masonry layout in Safari 26.4, math functions in the img sizes attribute, JavaScript Iterator.concat() sequencing, and the CloseWatcher interface in Firefox 149. Beta releases Chrome 147 and Firefox 150 preview contrast-color(), border-shape, element-scoped view transitions, revert-rule, and more.

recent_posts.title: January 2026 Baseline monthly digest
recent_posts.summary: The January 2026 Baseline digest covers web platform features that reached new milestones. Newly available features include the :active-view-transition CSS pseudo-class, JavaScript modules in service workers, the Navigation API for SPAs, and four new root-relative CSS units (rcap, rch, rex, ric). Widely available features include the multi-keyword CSS display property syntax, the animation-composition CSS property, and JavaScript's non-mutating array methods (toReversed, toSorted, toSpliced).

recent_posts.title: Navigation API - a better way to navigate, is now Baseline Newly Available
recent_posts.summary: The Navigation API has reached Baseline Newly Available status across all major browsers as of early 2026, replacing the long-problematic History API for single-page applications. It provides a single centralized NavigateEvent that handles all navigation types—link clicks, form submissions, back/forward buttons, and programmatic navigation—eliminating the fragile multi-step setup previously required. Key features include automatic URL updates, built-in accessibility handling (focus management), manual scroll timing control via event.scroll(), and seamless integration with the View Transitions API for app-like animations. Code examples demonstrate how the new API simplifies client-side routing compared to the old window.history approach.

recent_posts.title: New to the web platform in February
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of new web platform features landing in stable browsers during February 2026. Chrome 145 brings text-justify support, multicol column wrapping, customizable select listbox mode, Device Bound Session Credentials, and a new Origin API. Firefox 148 adds the shape() CSS function, Iterator.zip()/zipKeyed(), the HTML Sanitizer API, and overflow support on replaced elements. Safari 26.3 introduces Zstandard (Zstd) compression. Beta releases Chrome 146 and Firefox 149 preview scroll-triggered CSS animations, the Sanitizer API, popover hints, the Close Watcher API, and the Reporting API.

recent_posts.title: December 2025 Baseline monthly digest
recent_posts.summary: December 2025 saw several web platform features reach Baseline status. Newly available features include document.caretPositionFromPoint(), Event Timing API (for INP measurement), Largest Contentful Paint API, CSS scrollbar-color, scrollend event, CSS @scope, math font family, and invoker commands. Features reaching Widely available status include calc() keywords, JavaScript modules in workers, and window.print(). These milestones mean broader cross-browser support for important web APIs and styling capabilities.

recent_posts.title: New to the web platform in January
recent_posts.summary: Chrome 144 and Firefox 147 shipped in January 2026 with significant new features. CSS Anchor Positioning and the Navigation API became Baseline Newly available with Firefox 147. Chrome 144 added the Temporal API for modern date/time handling, the `::search-text` pseudo-element for find-in-page styling, a declarative `<geolocation>` HTML element, and the `caret-shape` CSS property. Firefox 147 enhanced View Transitions with type identification for SPAs. Beta releases Chrome 145 and Firefox 148 preview upcoming features including `text-justify`, multi-column improvements, and `Location.ancestorOrigins`.

recent_posts.title: Interop 2026: Continuing to improve the web for developers
recent_posts.summary: Interop 2026 is a cross-browser initiative led by Apple, Google, Igalia, Microsoft, and Mozilla to improve web platform feature consistency. The effort includes 20 focus areas based on developer surveys, covering CSS features like anchor positioning, container style queries, scroll-driven animations, and view transitions, plus APIs like Navigation API, WebTransport, and IndexedDB enhancements. Investigation efforts target accessibility testing, JPEG XL support, mobile testing infrastructure, and WebVTT improvements. Progress is tracked on a public dashboard with automated test results.
